speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned intense itching and red bumps on your thigh and elsewhere; can you describe how long these symptoms have been present and if they are itchy at night?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies. The combination of intense itching (often worse at night), new red bumps, recent travel to Miami, and a history of hypertension/diabetes suggests scabies, possibly with secondary bacterial infection or impetigo. I will ask you to confirm if you have had close contact with anyone else who is also itchy.
